national_raw_news.title: 2 hours ago | International 100 Riyadh airport hit again, Dammam also targeted; an Indian injured in Saturday’s attack dies
national_raw_news.content: Saudi Arabia’s King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh was targeted in another attack on Sunday, with the General Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA) saying that assessments of injuries and damage were underway. The latest incident came a day after Saturday’s attack on the airport, one of the deadliest in Saudi Arabia in almost a decade. Earlier, the Saudi-led coalition said that air defences had intercepted and destroyed a cruise missile near King Khalid International Airport. The coalition also reported that Terminal 4 at the airport had been hit by an unidentified projectile, triggering a fire. Separately, GACA said that King Fahd International Airport in Dammam was also targeted on Sunday evening. Damage assessments and safety inspections were underway. The Indian Embassy in Riyadh said on Sunday that an Indian national, among the 11 Indians injured in Saturday’s attack on King Khalid International Airport, had died. The Embassy expressed condolences to the bereaved family and said it was in touch with them to provide all possible assistance, including support for the early repatriation of the mortal remains. External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar expressed grief over the death and offered condolences to the bereaved family. He said the Embassy was extending all possible assistance and doing everything necessary to support those affected during this difficult time. The Indian Embassy said it had been monitoring the condition of the injured since the attack and had contacted local authorities and hospital officials to check on their well-being. Embassy officials also visited the hospitals where the injured Indians were admitted. In its latest update, the Embassy said three injured Indians were in intensive care but stable, two others remained admitted in regular wards, and the remaining injured had been discharged. Meanwhile, Yemen’s Houthi group claimed that it had carried out four missile and drone operations against Saudi targets in response to what it described as Saudi aggression against Yemen. According to a report by the Houthi-run Saba news agency, the claimed targets included King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, the Shugadam gas facility and Tanajib oil refinery in Saudi Arabia’s Eastern Province, and King Fahd International Airport in Dammam. The Houthis also warned international companies, aviation workers and travellers against operating flights to Saudi airports, claiming that they were unsafe, while exempting airports and airspace serving Mecca and Medina. Meanwhile, Yemen’s government armed forces, aligned with the internationally recognised government, said they had carried out 1,732 targeting operations, neutralised more than 900 Houthi fighters, and destroyed or disabled more than 287 military vehicles and other assets under their “Dawn of Yemen” operation.

national_raw_news.title: 2 hours ago | International 58 139 Migrants, Including 15 Children, Die as Boat Capsizes off Djibouti coast
national_raw_news.content: The International Organization for Migration (IOM) has said that 139 people, including 15 children, have died after an overcrowded boat carrying 305 migrants capsized near Guhere, north of Obock, off the coast of Djibouti in East Africa. The IOM reported that the vessel sank close to the shore shortly after departing on Thursday night. The official death toll stands at 139. However, IOM Chief of Mission in Djibouti, Alexandre Coissac, clarified that the figure includes only those whose bodies were buried by local authorities, while other victims were buried directly by migrants. 84 people remain missing as search-and-rescue operations continue, and the agency has warned that the death toll could rise. More than 80 survivors, all Ethiopian nationals, were rescued. Local authorities moved them to the IOM Rescue Centre in Obock, where they are receiving psychological support and medical care. The boat was travelling across the Bab el-Mandeb Strait from Djibouti to Yemen. This route is part of a popular but highly dangerous migration corridor used by tens of thousands of people from the Horn of Africa seeking work and safety in Gulf countries. According to the IOM’s Missing Migrants Project, more than 900 migrants died or went missing along this route last year alone.

national_raw_news.title: Two-day special voter enrolment drive concludes across Jammu and Kashmir 1 hour ago 32
national_raw_news.content: The two-day Special Intensive Voter Enrolment Drive concluded across Jammu and Kashmir yesterday, receiving a strong response from electors. Election officials undertook extensive outreach to facilitate voter registration, address public grievances and raise awareness about electoral services. Organised on October 10 and 11, the drive was conducted at polling stations across the Union Territory from 9 AM to 5 PM on both days. It provided eligible citizens with an opportunity to enrol as voters, seek corrections or updates to their electoral details, and obtain assistance with voter registration and related matters. The drive was guided by the Election Commission of India’s objective of ensuring that “No Eligible Voter is Left Behind”. The drive was conducted under the overall supervision of Chief Electoral Officer, Jammu and Kashmir, Sanjeev Verma. The district election machinery coordinated arrangements and facilitated enrolment services across the Union Territory. District Election Officers, Electoral Registration Officers, Deputy Directors of Information (Nodal Officers, SVEEP), Assistant Electoral Registration Officers and Election Naib Tehsildars (ENTs) oversaw the exercise in their respective jurisdictions. Booth Level Officers (BLOs) played a key role in assisting electors at polling stations and at the grassroots level. During the drive, grievances and queries raised by electors were taken up by the concerned election officials for redressal and appropriate action. The Election Department reiterated that the election machinery across Jammu and Kashmir remains available round the clock to assist the public, address grievances and provide guidance on voter enrolment and other electoral matters. Door-to-door outreach and inspections by election officers and other functionaries were also key components of the drive, helping identify and reach eligible voters and encouraging them to make use of the enrolment facilities.
